# Two Different Mechanisms in the Acid Rain Program

Under Title IV, the EPA’s Acid Rain Program addressed sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides from the power sector, but it did not apply one shared emissions rule to both pollutants.

For sulfur dioxide, the program used an aggregate cap and tradable allowances. Each allowance covered one ton of sulfur dioxide, while the cap set the permitted total; it was not a report of actual emissions. Coverage developed in phases. Phase I began in 1995 with 263 units at 110 plants. Substitution or compensating units brought the Phase I total to 445 units. Phase II began in 2000, and the final cap in 2010 was 8.95 million tons.

The nitrogen oxides component followed a different timeline and mechanism. Beginning in 1996, it applied a rate-based rule to certain coal-fired units, without introducing a cap or allowance trading. The two pollutants were therefore addressed through distinct rules, with different timelines.
